default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-458.title: Recent same-clock window drift follow
E-458.hypothesis: Index flows repeat at the same clock times (index arbitrage, institutional schedules); when the average move over the same clock window of the last 5 sessions is large and today's move agrees, follow it.

E-459.title: Robust median/MAD stretch fade
E-459.hypothesis: A price far from its rolling median in mean-absolute-deviation units is stretched by a few aggressive orders, not by a shift in value; liquidity providers pull it back.

E-460.title: Up-close share extreme fade
E-460.hypothesis: When nearly every close in a window is up and the price sits at the window high, buyers are exhausted (one-sided tape); fade the first such bar.

E-461.title: Range-burst direction follow
E-461.hypothesis: When the short-term average bar range jumps well above the hourly average, an informed order is working; follow the colour of the bar that makes the burst start.

E-462.title: Rolling-sigma shock bar fade
E-462.hypothesis: A single bar return far beyond the recent bar-return sigma is usually a sweep of thin liquidity that partly reverses; fade it.

E-463.title: Counter-position window break fade
E-463.hypothesis: A break of the recent window extreme against the session's location (rally breaks near the day low, dip breaks near the day high) is a counter-trend push; the larger flow resumes.

E-464.title: Jump-dominated move fade
E-464.hypothesis: A move driven by one outsized bar rather than steady pressure is a liquidity gap or a single order; it tends to retrace, unlike gradual moves.

E-465.title: EMA-Keltner stretch fade
E-465.hypothesis: Price beyond an EMA by several average bar ranges is overextended relative to its own trend; sellers or buyers of the other side step in.

E-466.title: US cash-open drive follow
E-466.hypothesis: The US cash open (10:30 or 11:30 in Sao Paulo time depending on daylight saving) brings foreign flow to the index; a larger-than-usual first move after it tends to be followed.

E-467.title: Bollinger band re-entry fade
E-467.hypothesis: A close back inside a Bollinger band after an excursion means the push failed; mean reversion toward the band centre follows.
